issues.t: Coolant loss and white smoke from oil cooler or EGR cooler failure
issues.sym: Coolant disappears with no puddle, white steam-like smoke comes from the tailpipe (worst at startup), coolant gets pushed out of the overflow (degas) bottle, or the engine runs hot when towing.
issues.why: The 6.0L's engine oil cooler clogs on the coolant side, which starves the EGR cooler of coolant. The overheated EGR cooler then cracks and lets coolant into the exhaust or intake. Owners report major repairs when it leads to head gasket damage.
issues.next: Watch the coolant level and compare engine oil and coolant temperatures with a scan tool; a gap of more than about 15 degrees points to a clogged oil cooler. Fix it early, before it damages the head gaskets.

issues.t: Head gaskets blow on the 6.0L diesel
issues.sym: Coolant pushed out of the overflow bottle, bubbles in the coolant, white exhaust smoke, and overheating under load.
issues.why: The 6.0L uses stretch-type head bolts that can give way under heat and high cylinder pressure, especially after an EGR cooler failure or with performance tuning.
issues.next: Stop towing and have a cooling system pressure test done. The lasting fix is new head gaskets with stronger head studs, along with fixing whatever caused the overheating.

issues.t: Spark plug blows out of the cylinder head
issues.sym: A sudden loud popping or ticking from the engine, a misfire and loss of power, and sometimes a broken ignition coil hanging loose.
issues.why: The 5.4L V8 and 6.8L V10 of this era have only a few threads holding each spark plug in the aluminum head. Over time a plug can work loose and shoot out, stripping the threads.
issues.next: Pull over and shut off the engine; driving on with a blown plug can damage the coil and wiring. A shop can install a thread insert. Have the plugs torqued properly at every tune-up.

issues.t: 6.0L diesel won't start from a failing injector control module
issues.sym: Hard starting or cranking with no start (often in cold weather), rough idle, misfiring and stalling.
issues.why: The fuel injection control module (FICM) on top of the engine powers the injectors. Engine heat, vibration and weak batteries wear out its electronics until it can't fire the injectors properly.
issues.next: Have the batteries tested first, then have a shop check the FICM output voltage. A rebuilt or upgraded FICM usually fixes the no-start.

issues.t: 6.0L diesel hard to start when hot from high-pressure oil leaks
issues.sym: Long cranking, no start when the engine is hot, or stalling, sometimes with codes P2284, P2285 or P2290/P2291.
issues.why: The 6.0L uses high-pressure engine oil to fire the injectors. Leaking O-rings at the oil rail plugs, standpipes or the pump fitting (STC fitting) let pressure bleed off, so the injectors can't fire.
issues.next: Have a diesel shop read injection control pressure while cranking. Leaking fittings and O-rings are fixable without replacing the pump in many cases.

issues.t: Turbo lag from sticking turbo vanes
issues.sym: Slow response when you press the gas, low boost, or a sudden surge of power once the turbo catches up.
issues.why: The 6.0L's variable-geometry turbo has vanes that stick from soot buildup, especially in trucks that do a lot of short trips and idling.
issues.next: Regular highway driving with a few hard pulls helps keep vanes clean. If lag persists, a shop can clean the vanes and unison ring.

issues.t: Rough cold running from sticking injectors (stiction)
issues.sym: The engine runs rough, misses or smokes on cold starts, then smooths out as it warms up.
issues.why: Deposits from engine oil make the 6.0L's oil-fired injectors stick internally. Long oil change intervals and poor oil make it worse.
issues.next: Change the oil on time with the correct diesel oil. Additives can help mild cases; badly sticking injectors need replacing.

issues.t: 6.0L diesel may stall without warning (recall)
issues.sym: The engine dies while driving and may not restart.
issues.why: Ford recalled 2004–2005 Excursions and other trucks with the 6.0L diesel because the engine could stall unexpectedly.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls; the dealer repair is free.

issues.t: Camshaft position sensor can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls without warning, cranks but won't start, and the tachometer may drop to zero.
issues.why: A failing camshaft position sensor stops sending the engine-speed signal, so the diesel shuts off or won't fire. Ford recalled about 1.2 million trucks and vans for this, including these Excursions.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A new sensor is a common fix even if the recall was done.

issues.t: 7.3L diesel misfires from injector wiring
issues.sym: Rough running or a miss on one or two cylinders, sometimes on and off, and hard starting.
issues.why: The wiring harness under each valve cover gets brittle from heat, and its connectors loosen. Less often, the injector driver module fails.
issues.next: Have a diesel shop check the under-valve-cover harness and connectors before replacing injectors.

issues.t: 7.3L diesel hard start or stalling from pressure sensor or regulator
issues.sym: Long cranking (especially hot), surging, rough idle or stalling, sometimes with oil seen on a sensor plug.
issues.why: The injection control pressure (ICP) sensor and injection pressure regulator (IPR) valve control oil pressure for the injectors. Leaking O-rings or failing sensors upset that pressure.
issues.next: Have the ICP and IPR checked with a scan tool. Unplugging a bad ICP sensor sometimes improves running temporarily; replace it with a new sensor.

issues.t: Exhaust smell and power loss from leaking turbo up-pipes
issues.sym: An exhaust smell in the cab, black soot near the back of the engine, and slow turbo response.
issues.why: The pipes that carry exhaust from the manifolds to the turbo have seals that blow out, so exhaust escapes before reaching the turbo.
issues.next: Have the up-pipes inspected. Upgraded welded up-pipes are a lasting fix; it is labor-heavy but cures the smell and power loss.

issues.t: 7.3L diesel hard to start in the cold from glow plugs
issues.sym: Long cranking on cold mornings, rough running, and white smoke until the engine warms up.
issues.why: Worn glow plugs, a failing glow plug relay, or bad connections under the valve covers mean the cylinders aren't warmed enough for a cold start.
issues.next: Have the glow plugs and relay tested. Replace the glow plugs as a set and check the relay at the same time.

issues.t: Automatic transmission overheats and fails
issues.sym: Slipping, harsh or delayed shifts, a burnt fluid smell, or the transmission quitting altogether, especially when towing.
issues.why: The 4R100 four-speed automatic in gas and 7.3L diesel Excursions runs hot when it hauls this much weight. Heat breaks down the fluid and wears out clutches. Owners report major repairs around 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Change the transmission fluid and filter regularly, more often if you tow. If shifts slip, stop towing and see a transmission shop before the damage spreads.

issues.t: Brakes shake, pull or wear rotors fast
issues.sym: Vibration through the steering wheel or pedal when braking, pulling to one side in hard stops, and rotors that need replacing often.
issues.why: The Excursion is very heavy for its brakes, so the rotors overheat and warp. Hundreds of owners complained about vibration, pulling and repeated rotor work.
issues.next: Use quality pads and rotors and have the calipers checked for sticking. Leave extra stopping distance, especially when loaded or towing.

issues.t: Cruise control switch can overheat and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Often no warning. Some owners notice cruise control that stops working, a burning smell, or brake fluid near the master cylinder.
issues.why: The speed control deactivation switch on the brake master cylinder can leak brake fluid internally, overheat and start a fire even with the engine off. Ford recalled millions of vehicles.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. Until it's fixed, park outside and away from buildings.

issues.t: Power door locks stop working
issues.sym: One or more doors won't lock or unlock with the switch or remote, the door makes a grinding noise, or the alarm acts up.
issues.why: The door lock actuators wear out, or resistance builds up in the wiring.
issues.next: Have the circuit tested first, then replace the bad actuator. Lock that door by hand until it's fixed.

issues.t: Lights can fail from the steering column switch (recall)
issues.sym: Headlights, turn signals or other exterior lights stop working.
issues.why: Ford recalled these Excursions because the multifunction switch on the steering column could fail and leave lights not working.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the repair is free.

issues.t: Battery ground wire can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or melted strap near the engine.
issues.why: A loose battery ground connection to the engine could overheat a radio suppression strap and cause melting or fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the repair is free.

issues.t: Headlight switch may be hard to turn on (recall)
issues.sym: The headlights are hard to switch on or don't come on.
issues.why: Ford recalled 2000 Excursions for a headlamp switch problem.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls.

issues.t: Windshield wipers can stop (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers stop working, possibly in rain.
issues.why: Water could get past the wiper motor cover and damage the motor. Ford recalled these trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls.

issues.t: Seat belt buckles may not latch fully (recall)
issues.sym: A buckle may seem latched but release, or may not latch properly.
issues.why: Ford recalled some 2001 vehicles because their TRW buckles might not restrain occupants properly in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the repair is free.

issues.t: Driver airbag may not deploy correctly (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before a crash.
issues.why: Ford recalled a small number of 2001 Excursions because the driver airbag module might not deploy properly or could cause burns.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the repair is free.

issues.t: Paint peels off
issues.sym: The paint or clear coat flakes and peels, often on the roof, hood and other sun-exposed panels.
issues.why: The factory paint layers lose adhesion over time, especially in strong sun.
issues.next: Wash and wax regularly to slow it down. Peeling panels need to be stripped and repainted.
